questions.q: The vehicles carrying inflammable fluids usually have metallic chains touching the ground :
options: To protect tyres from catching dirt from ground
To conduct excess charge due to air friction to ground and prevent sparking
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Static charge is developed due to air friction. This can result in combustion. So, metallic chains is used to discharge excess charge.

questions.q: As shown in the figure, a point charge Q is placed at the centre of conducting spherical shell of inner radius a and outer radius b. The electric field due to charge Q in three different regions I, II and III is given by : (I : r < a, II : a < r < b, III : r > b)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In region I, due to charge at centre, electric field will be present.

But in region II, electric field will be zero as electric field inside material of conductor is zero.

Again for outside region, net charges enclosed is not zero and therefore electric field will exist.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As r→·p→=0, this means that r→ is perpendicular to p→.

questions.q: Two point charges <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> each are placed at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> apart. A third point charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>q</mi></math> is placed at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> from mid-point on the perpendicular bisector. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> at which charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>q</mi></math> will experience the maximum Coulomb's force is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The distance between q and Q is r=x2+d22=x2+d24.

The force between q and Q will be F=kqQr2.

From the given figure we can see that only vertical components of the forces will add, and the horizontal components will get cancelled out. Therefore,

Fnet=2kqQr2cosθ=2kqQr2×xr=kqQxx2+d2432

For force to be maximum, dFnetdx=0.

⇒kqQx2+d2432-x×32x2+d2412×2xx2+d24322=0

⇒x2+d24=3x2⇒2x2=d24⇒x=d22

questions.q: A simple pendulum of length L is placed between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor having electric field  E , as shown in figure. Its bob has mass m and charge  q . The time period of the pendulum is given by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Two forces will be acting on the mass m, gravity force and force by the electric field.

Thus, the effective force =  qE2+mg2
From force equation, geff=g2+qEm2
Time period of the pendulum is T=2πLgeff
=2π Lg2+qEm2

questions.q: Two charges of each magnitude 0.01 C and separated by a distance of 0.4 mm constitute an electric dipole. If the dipole is placed in an uniform electric field E→ of 10 dyne·C-1 making 30∘ angle with E→, the magnitude of torque acting on dipole is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the dipole moment is given by

p⇀=qd⇀   ...1

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the dipole moment.

p⇀=0.01 C×0.4 mm×1 m103 mm= 4.0×10-6 C·m

The formula to calculate the torque on the dipole in the electric field is given by

|τ→|=|p→×E→|   ...2

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (2) to calculate the required torque.

τ⇀= 4.0×10-6 C·m×10 dyne·C-1× 1 N105 dyne×sin30°= 2×10-10 N m

questions.q: Concentric metallic hollow spheres of radii R and 4R hold charges <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> respectively. Given that surface charge densities of the concentric spheres are equal, the potential difference <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mfenced><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>)</mo></math> is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As given the surface charge density for both the spheres is same, hence

     σ1=σ2∴Q1A1=Q2A2⇒Q14πR2=Q24π4R2∴Q2=16Q1

From above diagram, the electric potential for both the spheres is 

VInner=KQ1R+KQ24R=KRQ1+16Q14=5KQ1R.

In the same way for outer sphere, 

VOuter=KQ14R+KQ24R=K4R16Q1+Q1=17KQ14R.

Now the potential difference is,

∆V=Vinner-Vouter

=5KQ1R-17KQ14R=3Q116πε0R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\tau=P E_0 \sin \theta$ If $\theta$ is small $\begin{aligned} \tau & =-\left(P E_0\right) \theta \\ I & =m\left(\frac{l}{2}\right)^2 \cdot 2=\frac{m l^2}{2} \\ T & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{m l^2}{2 \cdot P E_0}}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{m l^2}{2 \cdot q / E_0}} \\ T & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{m l}{2 q E_0}} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Which of the following correctly represents the variation of electric potential <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>V</mi><mo>)</mo></math> of a charged spherical conductor of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>)</mo></math> with radial distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></math> from the centre?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As electric field inside the charged conducting sphere is zero, therefore potential will be constant for the inside part.

For outside part, electric potential decreases as V=kqr and the conducting sphere behaves like a point charge concentrated at the centre.

questions.q: For a short dipole placed at origin $O$, the dipole moment $P$ is along $x$-axis, as shown in the figure. If the electric potential and electric field at A are $\mathrm{V}_0$ and $\mathrm{E}_0$, respectively, then the correct combination of the electric potential and electric field, respectively, at point $B$ on the $y$-axis is given by
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At point $A$ (axial)
$\left|E_0\right|=\frac{2 k_p}{r^3}, V_0=\frac{k_p}{r^2}$

At point $B$ (equatorial)
$\begin{aligned}
& |E|=\frac{k_p}{(2 r)^3}=\frac{E_0}{16} \\
& V=0
\end{aligned}$

Number of lines of force per unit area = electric field at surface=KQR2

E=ρR3ϵ0=2×63×8.85×10-12=0.45×1012 N C-1

questions.q:
A positive ion $A$ and a negative ion $B$ has charges $6.67 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}$ and $9.6 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{C}$, and masses $19.2 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{~kg}$ and $9 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{~kg}$ respectively. At an instant, the ions are separated by a certain distance r. At that instant the ratio of the magnitudes of electrostatic force to gravitational force is $P \times 10^{45}$, where the value of 10$P$ is $\qquad$
(Take $\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0}=9 \times 10^9 \mathrm{Nm}^2 \mathrm{C}^{-1}$ and universal gravitational constant as $6.67 \times 10^{-11} \mathrm{Nm}^2 \mathrm{~kg}^{-2}$ )
Assume that charge may not be an integral multiple of electrons.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
F_e & =\frac{k q_1 q_2}{r^2} \\
F_g & =\frac{G m_1 m_2}{r^2} \\
\frac{F_e}{F_g} & =\frac{k q_1 q_2}{G m_1 m_2} \\
& =\frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 6.67 \times 10^{-19} \times 9.6 \times 10^{-10}}{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 19.2 \times 10^{-27} \times 9 \times 10^{-27}} \\
& =\frac{10^{-20}}{2 \times 10^{-65}}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An electron revolves around an infinite cylindrical wire having uniform linear charge density 2×10-8 C m-1 in circular path under the influence of attractive electrostatic field as shown in the figure. The velocity of electron with which it is revolving is ______________ ×106 m s-1. Given mass of electron =9×10-31 kg
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The electric field is given by 

E=2kλr

The required centripetal force is 

F=mv2r

The force due to the field is equal to the required centripetal force,

⇒2kλre=mv2r

⇒v=2kλem=2×9×109×2×10-8×1.6×10-199×10-31

=1.6×4×1013=4×2×106 m s-1

= 8 × 106 m s-1

questions.q: Two charges of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>μC</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>μC</mi></math> are placed at the points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> located in an electric field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>E</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>20</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The magnitude of the torque acting on the dipole is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><msqrt><mi>α</mi></msqrt><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo></math>_________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given the electric field is

E→=0.20 i^ Vcm=20i^ Vm

The formula for calculating the torque is

τ→=p→×E→   ...1

where,

p→=ql→=4×2i^+-1j^+5k^-1i^+0j^+4k^=4i^-j^+k^ μC m

Thus, from equation (1), it follows that

τ→=(4i^-4j^+4k^)×10-6×(20i^) N m=(8k^+8j^)×10-5 N m⇒τ→=82+82×10-5 N m=82×10-5 N m

Hence, α=2.
